Question 1 of 20
  1. 1

    The segment of a number line from 000 to 111 is divided into 777 equal steps. Which fraction sits at the third mark counting from 000?

    Answer choices for question 1

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Writes the number of steps in the whole on top and the number of steps counted underneath, reversing the two jobs.

    You chose B: Puts the number of steps still to come, 7−3=47 - 3 = 47−3=4, under the bar instead of the number of steps in the whole.

    You chose D: Names the mark by its position number as a unit fraction, as though the third mark were one third.

    The denominator records how many equal steps the whole was cut into, and the numerator counts how many of those steps you take. Seven steps make the whole, and you take three of them.

    37=17+17+17\frac{3}{7} = \frac{1}{7} + \frac{1}{7} + \frac{1}{7}73​=71​+71​+71​

    So the third mark is three sevenths, and it lands before 111 because 333 is smaller than 777.

  2. 2

    What is 411+511\frac{4}{11} + \frac{5}{11}114​+115​?

    Answer choices for question 2

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Adds the denominators as well as the numerators, as though putting two groups of elevenths together made the pieces smaller.

    You chose C: Multiplies the two counts instead of adding them, while correctly leaving the piece size alone.

    You chose D: Reads the plus as a times throughout, multiplying the tops together and the bottoms together.

    Both fractions count elevenths, so the pieces are already the same size. Count them: four elevenths and five more elevenths is nine elevenths, and the size of a piece never changed.

    411+511=4+511=911\frac{4}{11} + \frac{5}{11} = \frac{4 + 5}{11} = \frac{9}{11}114​+115​=114+5​=119​

    Since 999 and 111111 share no factor above 111, this is already in lowest terms.

  3. 3

    Write 507\frac{50}{7}750​ as a mixed number.

    Answer choices for question 3

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: Writes the remainder over the original numerator instead of over the denominator.

    You chose B: Takes one complete group too few, leaving a fraction part that has not been brought below one whole.

    You chose C: Swaps the two results of the division, using the remainder as the whole part and the quotient as the count of sevenths.

    The bar is a division, so divide the numerator by the denominator and read the two results. Seven sevenths make one whole, so the quotient counts complete wholes and the remainder counts the sevenths left over.

    50÷7=7 remainder 1,507=71750 \div 7 = 7 \text{ remainder } 1, \qquad \frac{50}{7} = 7\tfrac{1}{7}50÷7=7 remainder 1,750​=771​

    The denominator stays 777, because the pieces were never re-cut, and the remainder 111 is below 777, so the fraction part is proper.

  4. 4

    Which of these is 3660\frac{36}{60}6036​ written in lowest terms?

    Answer choices for question 4

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Divides both terms by the common factor 444 and stops, though 999 and 151515 still share a factor of 333, so this is not in lowest terms.

    You chose C: Divides the numerator by 222 and the denominator by 333, using different numbers top and bottom, which changes the value.

    You chose D: Divides by the greatest common factor correctly but writes the two results the wrong way up.

    Dividing the numerator and the denominator by their greatest common factor reaches lowest terms in a single division. The common factors of 363636 and 606060 are 1,2,3,4,61, 2, 3, 4, 61,2,3,4,6 and 121212, and the greatest is 121212.

    3660=36÷1260÷12=35\frac{36}{60} = \frac{36 \div 12}{60 \div 12} = \frac{3}{5}6036​=60÷1236÷12​=53​

    Now check that nothing is left: 333 and 555 share no factor above 111, so the fraction is finished.

  5. 5

    What is 49×67\frac{4}{9} \times \frac{6}{7}94​×76​, in lowest terms?

    Answer choices for question 5

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Adds the two tops and the two bottoms instead of multiplying them.

    You chose C: Turns the second fraction over before multiplying, which is the rule for dividing, not for multiplying.

    You chose D: Multiplies the two numerators but keeps the first denominator, leaving the second denominator out of the product.

    Multiplying needs no common denominator: the tops multiply to count the pieces you keep and the bottoms multiply to count the pieces in the new whole.

    49×67=4×69×7=2463=821\frac{4}{9} \times \frac{6}{7} = \frac{4 \times 6}{9 \times 7} = \frac{24}{63} = \frac{8}{21}94​×76​=9×74×6​=6324​=218​

    The last step divides top and bottom by their greatest common factor 333. Cancelling the 666 against the 999 first gives 43×27\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{2}{7}34​×72​ and the same answer with smaller numbers.

  6. 6

    Exactly one of these names no number at all. Which one?

    Answer choices for question 6

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Treats a zero anywhere in a fraction as fatal, though taking none of the seven parts is a perfectly good amount, namely 000.

    You chose B: Reads a numerator and denominator that match as cancelling each other into nothing, rather than as taking every part, which is one whole.

    You chose D: Reads a denominator of 111 as no cutting at all and so no fraction, though it names the whole number 777.

    Read each one as a division. A denominator of 000 asks what number times 000 gives 777, and nothing times 000 gives anything but 000, so there is no answer.

    07=0,77=1,71=7,70 is undefined\frac{0}{7} = 0, \qquad \frac{7}{7} = 1, \qquad \frac{7}{1} = 7, \qquad \frac{7}{0} \text{ is undefined}70​=0,77​=1,17​=7,07​ is undefined

    A numerator of 000 is allowed; a denominator of 000 is not, because you cannot cut a whole into zero parts.

  7. 7

    Which statement is true?

    Answer choices for question 7

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Compares the denominators alone and lets the smaller denominator win, although the numerators differ too.

    You chose C: Sees each numerator sitting three below its denominator and reads equal gaps as equal values.

    You chose D: Believes a pair sharing neither number cannot be compared, though rewriting both over a shared denominator always settles it.

    The two fractions share neither number, so rewrite both over a common denominator. The least common multiple of 111111 and 101010 is 110110110.

    811=80110,710=77110\frac{8}{11} = \frac{80}{110}, \qquad \frac{7}{10} = \frac{77}{110}118​=11080​,107​=11077​

    With the pieces now the same size, the counts decide, and 80>7780 > 7780>77. The cross products give the same verdict: 8×10=808 \times 10 = 808×10=80 against 11×7=7711 \times 7 = 7711×7=77.

  8. 8

    Which of these fractions lies between 111 and 222 on the number line?

    Answer choices for question 8

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: Writes the two numbers the other way round, landing on a value below 111.

    You chose B: Counts the wholes by comparing 191919 with 999 rather than with 181818, so it misses that nineteen ninths has passed 222.

    You chose C: Builds a fraction out of the two whole numbers named in the question instead of finding a value that lies between them.

    Count in ninths. Nine ninths reach 111 and eighteen ninths reach 222, so a fraction of ninths lies between 111 and 222 exactly when its numerator is between 999 and 181818.

    99=1,139 lies between,189=2\frac{9}{9} = 1, \qquad \frac{13}{9} \text{ lies between}, \qquad \frac{18}{9} = 299​=1,913​ lies between,918​=2

    Thirteen is between 999 and 181818, so 139\frac{13}{9}913​ is the one. It is improper, which is exactly what a value past 111 has to be.

  9. 9

    What is 225×1782\tfrac{2}{5} \times 1\tfrac{7}{8}252​×187​?

    Answer choices for question 9

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: Multiplies whole part by whole part and fraction part by fraction part, which throws away the two cross products a product of sums contains.

    You chose B: Converts each mixed number by adding the whole number to the numerator instead of multiplying by the denominator, giving 45\frac{4}{5}54​ and 88\frac{8}{8}88​.

    You chose C: Cancels the 121212 against the 151515, but both of those are numerators, so the top of the product shrinks with no matching change underneath.

    Convert both factors first, since the multiplication rule expects a single numerator over a single denominator. Multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator.

    225=125,178=158,125×158=18040=92=4122\tfrac{2}{5} = \frac{12}{5}, \qquad 1\tfrac{7}{8} = \frac{15}{8}, \qquad \frac{12}{5} \times \frac{15}{8} = \frac{180}{40} = \frac{9}{2} = 4\tfrac{1}{2}252​=512​,187​=815​,512​×815​=40180​=29​=421​

    Cancelling first is quicker: the 121212 pairs with the 888 and the 151515 pairs with the 555, leaving 31×32\frac{3}{1} \times \frac{3}{2}13​×23​.

  10. 10

    Rewritten with a denominator of 565656, the fraction 58\frac{5}{8}85​ has which numerator?

    Answer choices for question 10

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Adds to the numerator the amount the denominator gained, 56−8=4856 - 8 = 4856−8=48, instead of multiplying by what the denominator was multiplied by.

    You chose C: Adds the multiplier 777 to the numerator instead of multiplying the numerator by it.

    You chose D: Reports the multiplier itself rather than the new numerator it produces.

    Find what the old denominator was multiplied by to reach the new one, then do the same to the numerator, since cutting every part into the same number of pieces leaves the amount alone.

    8×7=56,58=5×78×7=35568 \times 7 = 56, \qquad \frac{5}{8} = \frac{5 \times 7}{8 \times 7} = \frac{35}{56}8×7=56,85​=8×75×7​=5635​

    The multiplier has to hit both numbers; changing only one of them would change the value.

  11. 11

    What is 710+38\frac{7}{10} + \frac{3}{8}107​+83​?

    Answer choices for question 11

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Adds the two tops and the two bottoms, which would make the pieces smaller merely because two groups were put together.

    You chose C: Writes each denominator as 404040 but leaves the numerators untouched, giving 740+340\frac{7}{40} + \frac{3}{40}407​+403​.

    You chose D: Multiplies the two fractions instead of adding them, multiplying across the tops and the bottoms.

    Tenths and eighths are different sizes, so rebuild both over a shared size first. The least common multiple of 101010 and 888 is 404040.

    710=2840,38=1540,2840+1540=4340\frac{7}{10} = \frac{28}{40}, \qquad \frac{3}{8} = \frac{15}{40}, \qquad \frac{28}{40} + \frac{15}{40} = \frac{43}{40}107​=4028​,83​=4015​,4028​+4015​=4043​

    Each rebuild multiplied top and bottom by the same number, so nothing moved. Since 434343 and 404040 share no factor above 111, the improper answer 4340\frac{43}{40}4043​ is finished.

  12. 12

    What is 59÷1027\frac{5}{9} \div \frac{10}{27}95​÷2710​?

    Answer choices for question 12

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Multiplies straight across without turning the divisor over, treating division as though it were multiplication.

    You chose B: Turns the first fraction over instead of the divisor, which delivers the reciprocal of the correct quotient.

    You chose D: Turns both fractions over before multiplying, rather than only the fraction being divided by.

    Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal, because a fraction times its reciprocal is 111. Leave the first fraction alone and flip only the divisor.

    59÷1027=59×2710=13590=32\frac{5}{9} \div \frac{10}{27} = \frac{5}{9} \times \frac{27}{10} = \frac{135}{90} = \frac{3}{2}95​÷2710​=95​×1027​=90135​=23​

    Cancelling first is lighter: the 272727 pairs with the 999 and the 555 pairs with the 101010. The answer is above 111, which fits, since 1027\frac{10}{27}2710​ is smaller than 59\frac{5}{9}95​ and so fits into it more than once.

  13. 13

    Which list runs from least to greatest?

    Answer choices for question 13

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Orders by the size of the numbers written, putting the pair of smallest numbers first.

    You chose C: Orders by the gap between the two numbers of each fraction, 333, then 222, then 111, as though a wider gap meant a smaller value.

    You chose D: Compares the three correctly but lists them from greatest to least.

    No two of the three share a number, so neither glance-shortcut applies and each pair has to be rebuilt over a shared denominator. For 57\frac{5}{7}75​ against 811\frac{8}{11}118​ that denominator is 777777.

    57=5577,811=5677,so57<811\frac{5}{7} = \frac{55}{77}, \qquad \frac{8}{11} = \frac{56}{77}, \qquad \text{so} \qquad \frac{5}{7} < \frac{8}{11}75​=7755​,118​=7756​,so75​<118​

    The cross products are that same rebuild with the shared denominator left unwritten: 555555 and 565656 are exactly the products 5×115 \times 115×11 and 7×87 \times 87×8. So they settle the other two pairs in one line each.

    3×7=21>4×5=20,3×11=33>4×8=323 \times 7 = 21 > 4 \times 5 = 20, \qquad 3 \times 11 = 33 > 4 \times 8 = 323×7=21>4×5=20,3×11=33>4×8=32

    Those give 34>57\frac{3}{4} > \frac{5}{7}43​>75​ and 34>811\frac{3}{4} > \frac{8}{11}43​>118​, so the order is 57,811,34\frac{5}{7}, \frac{8}{11}, \frac{3}{4}75​,118​,43​.

  14. 14

    Where does 387\frac{38}{7}738​ sit?

    Answer choices for question 14

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: Writes the remainder over the original numerator instead of over the denominator, which shrinks the leftover almost to nothing.

    You chose B: Counts one complete group too many and takes the shortfall as the remainder: six sevens is 424242, which overshoots 383838 by 444.

    You chose C: Swaps the two results of the division, using the remainder as the whole part and the quotient as the count of sevenths.

    Counting in sevenths, every seven steps completes one whole, so divide the numerator by the denominator and read off both results.

    38÷7=5 remainder 3,387=53738 \div 7 = 5 \text{ remainder } 3, \qquad \frac{38}{7} = 5\tfrac{3}{7}38÷7=5 remainder 3,738​=573​

    Five complete wholes use up 353535 sevenths and three sevenths remain, so the point lies past 555 but short of 666, because three more sevenths do not reach a whole.

  15. 15

    What is 14÷7914 \div \frac{7}{9}14÷97​?

    Answer choices for question 15

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Multiplies by the fraction rather than by its reciprocal, so the divisor is never turned over.

    You chose B: Turns the 141414 over instead of the divisor, which delivers the reciprocal of the correct quotient.

    You chose D: Divides by the numerator 777 alone and ignores the denominator, as though the divisor were a whole number.

    Write the whole number over 111 and multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor, cancelling the shared 777 before multiplying.

    14÷79=141×97=21×91=1814 \div \frac{7}{9} = \frac{14}{1} \times \frac{9}{7} = \frac{2}{1} \times \frac{9}{1} = 1814÷97​=114​×79​=12​×19​=18

    The counting reading agrees. One whole holds 97\frac{9}{7}79​ of a piece of size 79\frac{7}{9}97​, so 141414 wholes hold 14×97=1814 \times \frac{9}{7} = 1814×79​=18 such pieces. The count is larger than 141414, which is what dividing by a number below 111 has to give.

  16. 16

    What is 614−2566\tfrac{1}{4} - 2\tfrac{5}{6}641​−265​?

    Answer choices for question 16

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Takes the smaller fraction from the larger in the fraction column, subtracting 312\tfrac{3}{12}123​ from 1012\tfrac{10}{12}1210​ the wrong way round.

    You chose C: Borrows a whole into the fraction column but forgets to take that whole away from the whole-number column.

    You chose D: Converts each mixed number by adding the whole number to the numerator instead of multiplying by the denominator, giving 74\frac{7}{4}47​ and 76\frac{7}{6}67​.

    Put the fraction parts over their least common denominator 121212, then look at the fraction column: 312\tfrac{3}{12}123​ is not enough to take 1012\tfrac{10}{12}1210​ from, so borrow one whole and add it as 1212\tfrac{12}{12}1212​.

    6312−21012=51512−21012=35126\tfrac{3}{12} - 2\tfrac{10}{12} = 5\tfrac{15}{12} - 2\tfrac{10}{12} = 3\tfrac{5}{12}6123​−21210​=51215​−21210​=3125​

    Converting instead gives the same thing: 254−176=7512−3412=4112\frac{25}{4} - \frac{17}{6} = \frac{75}{12} - \frac{34}{12} = \frac{41}{12}425​−617​=1275​−1234​=1241​.

  17. 17

    Exactly one of these has a value greater than 58\frac{5}{8}85​. Which one?

    Answer choices for question 17

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: Reads every multiplication as an increase, and picks the largest of the multipliers offered.

    You chose B: Reads every division as an increase, without checking whether the divisor sits above or below 111.

    You chose C: Sees the two 888s cancel and expects a product that loses its denominator to come out larger.

    Work each one out and compare it with 58\frac{5}{8}85​.

    58×910=916,58÷43=1532,58×89=59,58÷56=34\frac{5}{8} \times \frac{9}{10} = \frac{9}{16}, \quad \frac{5}{8} \div \frac{4}{3} = \frac{15}{32}, \quad \frac{5}{8} \times \frac{8}{9} = \frac{5}{9}, \quad \frac{5}{8} \div \frac{5}{6} = \frac{3}{4}85​×109​=169​,85​÷34​=3215​,85​×98​=95​,85​÷65​=43​

    Over a shared denominator of 288288288 those are 162162162, 135135135, 160160160 and 216216216, against 180180180 for 58\frac{5}{8}85​, so only the last is above it.

    The pattern behind that: for a positive starting number, multiplying by a fraction below 111 shrinks it and dividing by a fraction below 111 grows it. Three of the four second fractions here sit below 111, and only one of those three is a division.

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Converts both mixed numbers correctly but multiplies straight across without turning the divisor over.

    You chose B: Divides whole part by whole part and fraction part by fraction part, which a quotient of sums does not permit.

    You chose D: Turns the first fraction over instead of the divisor, which delivers the reciprocal of the correct quotient.

    Convert both mixed numbers first, then flip only the divisor.

    514=214,159=149,214÷149=214×9145\tfrac{1}{4} = \frac{21}{4}, \qquad 1\tfrac{5}{9} = \frac{14}{9}, \qquad \frac{21}{4} \div \frac{14}{9} = \frac{21}{4} \times \frac{9}{14}541​=421​,195​=914​,421​÷914​=421​×149​

    Cancel the 777 shared by 212121 and 141414, leaving 34×92=278\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{9}{2} = \frac{27}{8}43​×29​=827​, and 27÷8=327 \div 8 = 327÷8=3 remainder 333, so the answer is 3383\tfrac{3}{8}383​.

  19. 19

    What is 3−56−343 - \frac{5}{6} - \frac{3}{4}3−65​−43​?

    Answer choices for question 19

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: Combines the two fractions by adding the tops and the bottoms, using 810\frac{8}{10}108​ in place of their true total.

    You chose C: Writes the whole number as 312\frac{3}{12}123​, putting it over the common denominator without multiplying it by that denominator.

    You chose D: Carries the minus sign to the first fraction only and adds the second one.

    A whole number joins the calculation as a fraction over 111, rebuilt over the common denominator. The least common multiple of 666 and 444 is 121212, and 3=36123 = \frac{36}{12}3=1236​.

    Since 171717 and 121212 share no factor above 111, the answer is finished, and it is above 111, which fits: the two fractions taken away come to less than 222.

  20. 20

    A container holds 5565\tfrac{5}{6}565​ litres of juice. How many jugs of 712\frac{7}{12}127​ of a litre does it fill?

    Answer choices for question 20

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Multiplies the two amounts instead of asking how many of the smaller fit inside the larger.

    You chose C: Converts 5565\tfrac{5}{6}565​ by adding the whole number to the numerator instead of multiplying by the denominator, giving 106\frac{10}{6}610​.

    You chose D: Turns the first amount over rather than the divisor, which delivers the reciprocal of the correct count.

    "How many of these fit into that" is a division, so convert the mixed number and flip the divisor.

    556=356,356÷712=356×127=5×2=105\tfrac{5}{6} = \frac{35}{6}, \qquad \frac{35}{6} \div \frac{7}{12} = \frac{35}{6} \times \frac{12}{7} = 5 \times 2 = 10565​=635​,635​÷127​=635​×712​=5×2=10

    The 777 cancels into the 353535 and the 666 into the 121212. The count is larger than the number of litres, which is what dividing by an amount below one litre has to give.

Question 1 of 10
  1. 1

    1. A box measured in eighths . 12 points. Question 1 of 10.

    12 pts

    A charity collects tins in identical boxes. One box has been filled to 38\frac{3}{8}83​ of its capacity by 999 tins, and every eighth of the box holds the same number of tins as every other eighth.

    1. A
      Part A.

      How many tins does one full box hold? Show what the denominator asks you to do and what the numerator asks you to do.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 3 points

    2. B
      Part B.

      A second collection brings in 333333 tins. Write that as a fraction of one full box, in eighths. Say whether the fraction is proper or improper, give the pair of consecutive whole numbers it falls between, and write down the division the bar stands for.

      Carry your own answer forward Use the size of one eighth that follows from your answer to part A, whatever it came to, and work honestly from there.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 5 points

    3. C
      Part C.

      A third box of the same capacity is packed in three layers of unequal depth. The packer points at the bottom layer and calls it 13\frac{1}{3}31​ of the box, on the grounds that it is one of the three layers. Explain what naming a fraction requires that this description does not supply, and give a circumstance in which 13\frac{1}{3}31​ would be the right name for that layer.

      Explain why it works A sentence or two. Reasons, not steps. 4 points

    The answer

    Part A

    One full box holds 242424 tins.

    • 242424 tins, whether reached as 9÷3×89 \div 3 \times 89÷3×8 or by noting that 888 eighths is 83\frac{8}{3}38​ of the 999 tins

    Part B

    118\frac{11}{8}811​ of a box, an improper fraction lying between 111 and 222. The bar stands for 11÷811 \div 811÷8.

    Part C

    A fraction names equal parts of a whole, and three layers of unequal depth are not equal, so being one of three pieces does not establish the name. The description fails to prove it rather than to disprove it. The layer would be 13\frac{1}{3}31​ if all three layers were equal, or if it were measured and found to hold a third of the tins.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    The numerator 333 says the 999 tins are three equal eighths, so undo that count first to find one eighth.

    9÷3=3 tins in one eighth9 \div 3 = 3 \text{ tins in one eighth}9÷3=3 tins in one eighth

    The denominator 888 says a full box is eight of those equal parts.

    3×8=24 tins in a full box3 \times 8 = 24 \text{ tins in a full box}3×8=24 tins in a full box

    Part B

    One eighth of a box is 333 tins, so count how many eighths the 333333 tins make.

    33÷3=11 eighths,11833 \div 3 = 11 \text{ eighths}, \qquad \frac{11}{8}33÷3=11 eighths,811​

    The numerator is larger than the denominator, so the fraction is improper. Eight eighths make 111 and sixteen eighths make 222, and 111111 sits between 888 and 161616, so the value lies between 111 and 222. The bar is a division sign, so 118=11÷8\frac{11}{8} = 11 \div 8811​=11÷8.

    Part C

    The denominator does two jobs at once: it counts the pieces the whole was cut into and, by doing so, fixes how big each piece is. That second job only works when the pieces are equal.

    13 of a box=one of 3 EQUAL parts of the box\frac{1}{3} \text{ of a box} = \text{one of } 3 \text{ EQUAL parts of the box}31​ of a box=one of 3 EQUAL parts of the box

    Three layers of unequal depth are three pieces, but they are not three equal pieces, so "it is one of the three layers" is not a reason for calling it a third. The packer's argument is what fails.

    That is not the same as saying the layer is not a third. Equal layers would settle the name, but they are not the only thing that could. Three layers of 13\tfrac{1}{3}31​, 14\tfrac{1}{4}41​ and 512\tfrac{5}{12}125​ of a box fill it exactly, no two of them are equal, and the first is still exactly one third.

    13+14+512=412+312+512=1\tfrac{1}{3} + \tfrac{1}{4} + \tfrac{5}{12} = \tfrac{4}{12} + \tfrac{3}{12} + \tfrac{5}{12} = 131​+41​+125​=124​+123​+125​=1

    So there are two honest ways to earn the name here: repack so that all three layers hold the same amount, 888 tins each in a box of 242424; or measure this layer and find it holds 888 of the 242424 tins. What cannot earn it is counting the layers.

    Watch out. "One of three" and "one third" are different claims. The first is a count of pieces; the second is a measurement, and a measurement needs a fixed unit.

    In one line

    A full box holds 242424 tins, since 9÷3=39 \div 3 = 39÷3=3 tins in one eighth and 3×8=243 \times 8 = 243×8=24. The second collection of 333333 tins is 111111 eighths, that is 118\frac{11}{8}811​ of a box, an improper fraction lying between 111 and 222, and the bar stands for 11÷811 \div 811÷8. The packer's reason is what fails: a fraction names equal parts of a whole, and three layers of unequal depth give three pieces but not three equal ones, so counting the layers cannot earn the name. That does not settle the layer's size either way; unequal layers of 13\tfrac{1}{3}31​, 14\tfrac{1}{4}41​ and 512\tfrac{5}{12}125​ of a box fill it exactly and the first is still a third. The name would be right if all three layers held the same amount, 888 tins each, or if this layer were measured at 888 of the 242424 tins.

      Part C.

Decide whether 914\frac{9}{14}149​ equals 49\frac{4}{9}94​, support the decision with a calculation, and say how the building rule differs from what the classmate did.

      Justify your claim State the claim, then give the reason it has to be true. 4 points

    The answer

    Part A

    49=2045\frac{4}{9} = \frac{20}{45}94​=4520​, using the multiplier 555.

    • 2045\frac{20}{45}4520​, with or without the multiplier left showing as 4×59×5\frac{4 \times 5}{9 \times 5}9×54×5​

    Part B

    4270=35\frac{42}{70} = \frac{3}{5}7042​=53​, dividing both terms by 141414.

    Part C

    They are not equal: the cross products 4×14=564 \times 14 = 564×14=56 and 9×9=819 \times 9 = 819×9=81 differ. Multiplying both terms by one number cuts every part into that many pieces and counts that many more, leaving the amount alone. Adding matches no such re-cutting, and moves the value whenever the two terms differ.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Ask what the old denominator was multiplied by to reach the new one, then do the same on top.

    9×5=45,49=4×59×5=20459 \times 5 = 45, \qquad \frac{4}{9} = \frac{4 \times 5}{9 \times 5} = \frac{20}{45}9×5=45,94​=9×54×5​=4520​

    Watch out. Writing 445\frac{4}{45}454​ changes the denominator without paying for it on top. That is a different number, one fifth of the one asked for.

    Part B

    One division is enough when the number you divide by is the greatest common factor. The factors shared by 424242 and 707070 are 111, 222, 777 and 141414.

    GCF⁡(42,70)=14,4270=42÷1470÷14=35\operatorname{GCF}(42, 70) = 14, \qquad \frac{42}{70} = \frac{42 \div 14}{70 \div 14} = \frac{3}{5}GCF(42,70)=14,7042​=70÷1442÷14​=53​

    Check that nothing is left: 333 and 555 share no factor above 111, so the fraction is finished.

    Part C

    Settle the equality first, with cross products.

    4×14=56against9×9=814 \times 14 = 56 \qquad\text{against}\qquad 9 \times 9 = 814×14=56against9×9=81

    The two products differ, so the fractions are not equal. Rewriting both over 126126126 says the same thing: 49=56126\frac{4}{9} = \frac{56}{126}94​=12656​ and 914=81126\frac{9}{14} = \frac{81}{126}149​=12681​, so the classmate's fraction is the larger.

    The reason the building rule works is that multiplying by ccc describes an action on the picture: each of the 999 parts becomes ccc smaller pieces, so the whole holds 9c9c9c of them, and each of the 444 shaded parts becomes ccc pieces, so 4c4c4c are shaded. Nothing was added or removed, only cut lines drawn. Adding 555 to each term describes no such action: it does not cut the parts, it invents five more of them on top and five more underneath, and the shaded share changes.

    Watch out. "The same change to both" is not the test. The test is whether the change is one the picture can perform, and only multiplying and dividing are.

    In one line

    49=2045\frac{4}{9} = \frac{20}{45}94​=4520​, using the multiplier 555 on both terms, and 4270=35\frac{42}{70} = \frac{3}{5}7042​=53​ after one division by the greatest common factor 141414. The classmate is wrong: 4×14=564 \times 14 = 564×14=56 but 9×9=819 \times 9 = 819×9=81, so 914\frac{9}{14}149​ is not 49\frac{4}{9}94​. Multiplying both terms by the same number cuts every part into that many equal pieces and counts that many more of them, which leaves the amount exactly where it was; adding the same number to both matches no cutting at all, and moves the value whenever the two terms differ.

    Part B

Work out that subtraction, decide whether the claim holds, and say how the two results are related.

      Carry your own answer forward Compare against whatever difference you reported in part B, and say honestly how the two results are related.

      Justify your claim State the claim, then give the reason it has to be true. 5 points

    Part A

    3724\frac{37}{24}2437​ of a lap, over the least common denominator 242424, with multiplier 222 on 1112\frac{11}{12}1211​ and multiplier 333 on 58\frac{5}{8}85​.

    • 3724\frac{37}{24}2437​ of a lap, or the same amount written as the mixed number 113241\tfrac{13}{24}12413​ laps

    Part B

    The first stretch is longer by 724\frac{7}{24}247​ of a lap.

    Part C

    58−1112=−724\frac{5}{8} - \frac{11}{12} = -\frac{7}{24}85​−1211​=−247​, so the claim does not hold. The two results share the same distance from zero, 724\frac{7}{24}247​ of a lap, and differ in sign: reversing a subtraction gives the opposite, because subtraction is not commutative.

    Part A

    Twelfths and eighths are different sizes, so rebuild both over a shared size. The least common multiple of 121212 and 888 is 242424.

    1112=2224,58=1524\frac{11}{12} = \frac{22}{24}, \qquad \frac{5}{8} = \frac{15}{24}1211​=2422​,85​=2415​

    Now every piece is a twenty-fourth, so count them.

    2224+1524=3724\frac{22}{24} + \frac{15}{24} = \frac{37}{24}2422​+2415​=2437​

    Since 373737 is prime and does not divide 242424, the fraction is already in lowest terms. It is improper, which fits: the walker has passed one full lap.

    Watch out. Adding the denominators too, as 11+512+8=1620=45\frac{11 + 5}{12 + 8} = \frac{16}{20} = \frac{4}{5}12+811+5​=2016​=54​, returns less than the first stretch on its own, which no total of two positive lengths can be.

    The rebuilds from part A serve here too, since the pieces have to match for a subtraction just as they do for an addition.

    Since 777 and 242424 share no factor above 111, the answer is finished.

    Rebuild over 242424 again and subtract in the order written.

    58−1112=1524−2224=15−2224=−724\frac{5}{8} - \frac{11}{12} = \frac{15}{24} - \frac{22}{24} = \frac{15 - 22}{24} = -\frac{7}{24}85​−1211​=2415​−2422​=2415−22​=−247​

    "Of" is a multiplication, so the purchase is 56\frac{5}{6}65​ of 815\frac{8}{15}158​. Once the product is written as one fraction, any numerator may be cancelled against any denominator, whichever fraction each came from.

    ab÷cd=ab×dc=a×db×c,ba×cd=b×ca×d\frac{a}{b} \div \frac{c}{d} = \frac{a}{b} \times \frac{d}{c} = \frac{a \times d}{b \times c}, \qquad \frac{b}{a} \times \frac{c}{d} = \frac{b \times c}{a \times d}ba​÷dc​=ba​×cd​=b×ca×d​,ab​×dc​=a×db×c​

    The second is the first with its numerator and denominator swapped, so it is always the reciprocal of the correct quotient. Four numbers have to be nonzero for that sentence to mean anything, and each for its own reason: bbb and ddd because they are denominators, ccc because dividing by cd\frac{c}{d}dc​ is dividing by zero otherwise, and aaa because turning ab\frac{a}{b}ba​ over puts aaa underneath. That last one is also what gives the correct quotient a reciprocal to be.

    Watch out. A reciprocal-shaped answer is a useful alarm. A count of pieces that comes out below 111, when the pieces are smaller than the amount being cut up, is worth rechecking before it is written down.

    135×134=85×74=25×71=145=2451\tfrac{3}{5} \times 1\tfrac{3}{4} = \frac{8}{5} \times \frac{7}{4} = \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{7}{1} = \frac{14}{5} = 2\tfrac{4}{5}153​×143​=58​×47​=52​×17​=514​=254​

    That is the batch size the question began with, so the check passes.

    The reason it must pass is what division means. Writing QQQ for the count of moulds, the division in part B was solving

      Part C.

      A classmate says that 06\frac{0}{6}60​ must be smaller than 04\frac{0}{4}40​, because sixths are smaller pieces than quarters and both fractions take the same number of them. Decide whether that is right, and state any condition the same-numerator comparison needs before it may be used, saying whether the comparison holds once any such condition is met.

      Justify your claim State the claim, then give the reason it has to be true. 5 points

    The answer

    Part A

    57<34<1114\frac{5}{7} < \frac{3}{4} < \frac{11}{14}75​<43​<1411​, compared over the shared denominator 282828.

    • 57<34<1114\frac{5}{7} < \frac{3}{4} < \frac{11}{14}75​<43​<1411​ written as one chain, or as a list given in that order

    Part B

    06=0\frac{0}{6} = 060​=0 and 1515=1\frac{15}{15} = 11515​=1. In order: 06<57<34<1114<1515\frac{0}{6} < \frac{5}{7} < \frac{3}{4} < \frac{11}{14} < \frac{15}{15}60​<75​<43​<1411​<1515​.

    Part C

    It is not right: 06\frac{0}{6}60​ and 04\frac{0}{4}40​ are both 000, so they are equal. The comparison needs the shared numerator to be nonzero, because taking none of the parts gives nothing whatever their size. With a nonzero shared numerator it does work, and the smaller denominator names the larger fraction.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    No two of the three share a number, so neither glance-shortcut applies. Rebuild all three over a common denominator; the least common multiple of 777, 444 and 141414 is 282828.

    57=2028,34=2128,1114=2228\frac{5}{7} = \frac{20}{28}, \qquad \frac{3}{4} = \frac{21}{28}, \qquad \frac{11}{14} = \frac{22}{28}75​=2820​,43​=2821​,1411​=2822​

    Now every piece is a twenty-eighth, so the counts decide, and 20<21<2220 < 21 < 2220<21<22.

    Part B

    Read each one from the meaning of the two numbers. Taking none of six equal parts is nothing, and taking all fifteen of fifteen equal parts is the whole.

    06=0÷6=0,1515=15÷15=1\frac{0}{6} = 0 \div 6 = 0, \qquad \frac{15}{15} = 15 \div 15 = 160​=0÷6=0,1515​=15÷15=1

    The other three are proper fractions, so each lies strictly between 000 and 111, which places the two new entries at the two ends.

    06<57<34<1114<1515\frac{0}{6} < \frac{5}{7} < \frac{3}{4} < \frac{11}{14} < \frac{15}{15}60​<75​<43​<1411​<1515​

    Part C

    Evaluate both sides before arguing about them.

    06=0and04=0,so06=04\frac{0}{6} = 0 \qquad\text{and}\qquad \frac{0}{4} = 0, \qquad\text{so}\qquad \frac{0}{6} = \frac{0}{4}60​=0and40​=0,so60​=40​

    The classmate's reasoning has one true half and one missing condition. It is true that a sixth is a smaller piece than a quarter. It does not follow that the fractions differ, because neither fraction takes any pieces at all, and no number of nothing is bigger than any other number of nothing.

    So the shortcut has to be stated with its condition attached: when two fractions share the same nonzero numerator, the one with the smaller denominator is the larger, because the same count of bigger pieces is more.

    34>37,but04=07\frac{3}{4} > \frac{3}{7}, \qquad\text{but}\qquad \frac{0}{4} = \frac{0}{7}43​>73​,but40​=70​

    With the condition met the comparison is sound in both directions on that family: among fractions sharing one nonzero numerator, a smaller denominator gives a larger value and a larger value comes from a smaller denominator.

    Watch out. Zero is the only numerator that breaks it, and it breaks it completely: every fraction with numerator 000 equals every other one.

    In one line

    Over the shared denominator 282828 the three fractions are 2028\frac{20}{28}2820​, 2128\frac{21}{28}2821​ and 2228\frac{22}{28}2822​, so 57<34<1114\frac{5}{7} < \frac{3}{4} < \frac{11}{14}75​<43​<1411​. The two new entries are 06=0\frac{0}{6} = 060​=0 and 1515=1\frac{15}{15} = 11515​=1, which sit at the two ends because the others are proper fractions: 06<57<34<1114<1515\frac{0}{6} < \frac{5}{7} < \frac{3}{4} < \frac{11}{14} < \frac{15}{15}60​<75​<43​<1411​<1515​. The classmate is wrong, since 06\frac{0}{6}60​ and 04\frac{0}{4}40​ are both 000 and so equal. The shortcut holds only when the shared numerator is nonzero: taking none of the parts gives nothing whatever their size. With a nonzero shared numerator the smaller denominator does name the larger fraction.

      Part C.

    The answer

    Part A

    84126=23\frac{84}{126} = \frac{2}{3}12684​=32​, dividing both terms by 424242.

    Part B

    The correct value is 219=73\frac{21}{9} = \frac{7}{3}921​=37​. Striking the nines divided one term of the sum on top by 999 while dividing the whole of the bottom by 999, so the two halves of the fraction were not divided by the same thing, and the value jumped from about 2132\tfrac{1}{3}231​ to 121212.

    Part C

    It must be a factor of the whole numerator and of the whole denominator. In 9×129\frac{9 \times 12}{9}99×12​ the 999 is a factor of the numerator 108108108, so it divides out to leave 121212. In 9+129\frac{9 + 12}{9}99+12​ the numerator is 212121, which 999 does not divide, so nothing divides out.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Break both numbers into primes to read off the greatest common factor.

    84=2×2×3×7,126=2×3×3×784 = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 7, \qquad 126 = 2 \times 3 \times 3 \times 784=2×2×3×7,126=2×3×3×7

    The factors they share are one 222, one 333 and one 777, so the greatest common factor is 2×3×7=422 \times 3 \times 7 = 422×3×7=42.

    84126=84÷42126÷42=23\frac{84}{126} = \frac{84 \div 42}{126 \div 42} = \frac{2}{3}12684​=126÷4284÷42​=32​

    Check: 222 and 333 share no factor above 111, so one division was enough.

    Part B

    Work the numerator out before touching it.

    9+129=219=21÷39÷3=73\frac{9 + 12}{9} = \frac{21}{9} = \frac{21 \div 3}{9 \div 3} = \frac{7}{3}99+12​=921​=9÷321÷3​=37​

    So the true value is 73\frac{7}{3}37​, a little over 222, and the student's report of 121212 is more than five times too big.

    The move looks like a cancellation but is not one. Simplifying divides the whole numerator and the whole denominator by the same number, and the whole numerator here is 212121, which 999 does not divide at all. What the strike really did was replace 9+129 + 129+12 by 121212, that is, delete a term, while dividing the denominator by 999.

    Watch out. A quick size check catches it: the numerator is a little over twice the denominator, so the answer has to be a little over 222.

    Part C

    The rule is ab=a÷cb÷c\frac{a}{b} = \frac{a \div c}{b \div c}ba​=b÷ca÷c​, and it demands that ccc divide aaa and bbb exactly. Read it as an instruction about the two complete numbers, not about digits that happen to match.

    The product. The numerator is one number, 9×12=1089 \times 12 = 1089×12=108, and 999 is a factor of it, since 108=9×12108 = 9 \times 12108=9×12.

    9×129=108÷99÷9=121=12\frac{9 \times 12}{9} = \frac{108 \div 9}{9 \div 9} = \frac{12}{1} = 1299×12​=9÷9108÷9​=112​=12

    So here the cancellation is legal and gives exactly what the strike-out claimed.

    The sum. The numerator is 9+12=219 + 12 = 219+12=21, and 999 is not a factor of 212121: dividing gives 222 remainder 333.

    9+129=219=73\frac{9 + 12}{9} = \frac{21}{9} = \frac{7}{3}99+12​=921​=37​

    Being a term of a sum does not make a number a factor of it: here the numerator is 212121, which 999 does not divide, while in the product the numerator is 108108108, which it does. What decides it is the arithmetic, not the layout.

    In one line

    84126=23\frac{84}{126} = \frac{2}{3}12684​=32​ after one division by the greatest common factor 424242. The student's report of 121212 for 9+129\frac{9 + 12}{9}99+12​ is wrong: the numerator is 212121, so the value is 219=73\frac{21}{9} = \frac{7}{3}921​=37​, and the strike deleted a term of the sum rather than dividing the whole numerator. A number may be divided out only when it is a factor of the whole numerator and of the whole denominator. In 9×129\frac{9 \times 12}{9}99×12​ the nine is a factor of the numerator 108108108, so it divides out and leaves 121212; in 9+129\frac{9 + 12}{9}99+12​ it is one term of a sum and not a factor of 212121, so nothing divides out.

    Rubric

    Mark your own paper against this. Give yourself the points for each element you actually wrote down, not the ones you meant to.

  10. 10

    10. One sum, added twice . 13 points. Question 10 of 10.

    13 pts

    Two students add 715+49\frac{7}{15} + \frac{4}{9}157​+94​. One rewrites both fractions over the least common denominator. The other multiplies the two denominators together and rewrites both over that.

    1. A
      Part A.

      Carry out the first student's calculation. Give the denominator used and the total in lowest terms.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 3 points

    2. B
      Part B.

      Carry out the second student's calculation as well, all the way to lowest terms. Report the denominator used, the total before simplifying, and the total after.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 4 points

    3. C
      Part C.

      Before the second student's last division, the two of them hold totals that do not look alike. Decide whether either has gone wrong, explain what settles whether the two totals are the same number, and say what, if anything, the larger denominator cost.

      Carry your own answer forward Compare the two totals you actually produced in parts A and B, and argue from those.

      Justify your claim State the claim, then give the reason it has to be true. 6 points

    The answer

    Part A

    4145\frac{41}{45}4541​, over the least common denominator 454545.

    Part B

    Over the denominator 135135135 the total is 123135\frac{123}{135}135123​ before simplifying, which becomes 4145\frac{41}{45}4541​ after dividing both terms by 333.

    Part C

    Neither has gone wrong. Every rebuild multiplies top and bottom by the same nonzero number, so it is an equality and both students added the same two amounts. Indeed 123135\frac{123}{135}135123​ is 4145\frac{41}{45}4541​ with both terms times 333. The larger denominator cost only bigger numbers and a simplification still owed.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    The least common denominator is the least common multiple of the two denominators. Multiples of 151515 run 15,30,4515, 30, 4515,30,45, and 454545 is the first that 999 also divides.

    lcm⁡(15,9)=45,715=2145,49=2045\operatorname{lcm}(15, 9) = 45, \qquad \frac{7}{15} = \frac{21}{45}, \qquad \frac{4}{9} = \frac{20}{45}lcm(15,9)=45,157​=4521​,94​=4520​

    Now the pieces match, so add the counts.

    2145+2045=4145\frac{21}{45} + \frac{20}{45} = \frac{41}{45}4521​+4520​=4541​

    Since 414141 is prime and does not divide 454545, this is in lowest terms.

    Part B

    The product of the denominators is 15×9=13515 \times 9 = 13515×9=135, which is a common multiple of both, so both fractions can be rebuilt over it.

    715=63135,49=60135,63135+60135=123135\frac{7}{15} = \frac{63}{135}, \qquad \frac{4}{9} = \frac{60}{135}, \qquad \frac{63}{135} + \frac{60}{135} = \frac{123}{135}157​=13563​,94​=13560​,13563​+13560​=135123​

    That is not finished: 123=3×41123 = 3 \times 41123=3×41 and 135=3×45135 = 3 \times 45135=3×45, so both terms carry a factor of 333.

    123135=123÷3135÷3=4145\frac{123}{135} = \frac{123 \div 3}{135 \div 3} = \frac{41}{45}135123​=135÷3123÷3​=4541​

    Part C

    Take the steps one at a time. Each rebuild is an instance of the building rule, and the building rule is an equality, not an approximation.

    715=2145=63135,49=2045=60135\frac{7}{15} = \frac{21}{45} = \frac{63}{135}, \qquad \frac{4}{9} = \frac{20}{45} = \frac{60}{135}157​=4521​=13563​,94​=4520​=13560​

    So both students added the same two amounts, merely described in pieces of different sizes, and adding equal things to equal things gives equal results. Their totals must agree, and they do.

    123135=41×345×3=4145\frac{123}{135} = \frac{41 \times 3}{45 \times 3} = \frac{41}{45}135123​=45×341×3​=4541​

    What the choice of denominator affects is only the size of the numbers on the page. Any common multiple of 151515 and 999 can serve as the denominator, since each fraction has to be rebuildable over it, and 135135135 is one such multiple, just not the smallest. Choosing a bigger one describes the same answer in smaller pieces, so the numerators are larger, and it leaves behind a common factor that has to be divided out at the end. The least common denominator is preferred for that reason alone, not because the others are wrong.

    Watch out. "Different-looking" and "different" are not the same. Two fractions settle it by simplifying to a shared lowest-terms form, or by cross products: 41×135=553541 \times 135 = 553541×135=5535 and 45×123=553545 \times 123 = 553545×123=5535.

    In one line

    Over the least common denominator 454545 the sum is 2145+2045=4145\frac{21}{45} + \frac{20}{45} = \frac{41}{45}4521​+4520​=4541​. Over the product 135135135 it is 63135+60135=123135\frac{63}{135} + \frac{60}{135} = \frac{123}{135}13563​+13560​=135123​, which divides by 333 to give 4145\frac{41}{45}4541​ as well. Neither student has gone wrong: every rebuild multiplies top and bottom by the same nonzero number and so is an equality, meaning both added the same two amounts and had to reach the same value. The larger denominator cost only bigger numbers along the way and a simplification still owed at the end.

    Rubric

    Mark your own paper against this. Give yourself the points for each element you actually wrote down, not the ones you meant to.

    1

    Part B 4 points

    2

    Rebuilds both fractions over the product of the denominators and adds the numerators. . Worth 2 points.

    2

    Simplifies the total to lowest terms and reports both the unsimplified and the simplified form. . Worth 2 points.

    Part C 6 points

    3

    Clears both students and grounds the agreement in each rewriting step being an equality, so the same two amounts were added twice. . Worth 3 points. needs an explanation, not just an answer

    2

    Shows the two totals are one number, by the building rule between them, by a shared lowest-terms form, or by cross products. . Worth 2 points.

    1

    Names the cost of the larger denominator as bigger numbers and a simplification still owed, rather than as an error. . Worth 1 point.

Marking rubrics

Work every question first. Then mark your own paper against these, giving yourself the points for each element you actually wrote down.

1. A box measured in eighths 12 points

Part A 3

  • Divides by the numerator to find the size of one part and multiplies by the denominator to rebuild the whole, rather than the other way round. 2
  • Reports the result as a number of tins in one full box. 1

Part B 5

  • Counts the tins in eighths of a box and writes the count over the denominator 888. 2
  • Classifies the fraction by comparing numerator with denominator and names the two consecutive whole numbers it falls between. 2
  • Writes the fraction as a division with the numerator divided by the denominator, in that order. 1

Part C 4

  • Names the equal-parts requirement as what the packer's reasoning is missing, and ties it to the job the denominator does in fixing the size of a part. 3
  • Gives a circumstance under which the name would be correct, either three equal layers or this layer measured at a third of the box. 1

2. Two directions along the same rule 10 points

Part A 3

  • Identifies the multiplier from the two denominators and applies that same multiplier to the numerator. 2
  • Reports the equivalent fraction and names the multiplier used. 1

Part B 3

  • Divides the numerator and the denominator by the same number, and by the greatest of their common factors so that one division suffices. 2
  • Confirms the result has no common factor above 111 left, so it is in lowest terms. 1

Part C 4

  • Rejects the equality and supports it with a calculation, either the two cross products or the two fractions rewritten over a shared denominator. 2
  • Explains that multiplying both terms by the same number corresponds to cutting each part into equal pieces, and that adding corresponds to no such re-cutting. 2

3. There and back again 12 points

Part A 3

  • Divides numerator by denominator and reports both the quotient and the remainder. 2
  • Says which result counts whole units and which counts the leftover pieces, naming the pieces by the denominator. 1

Part B 4

  • Multiplies the whole number by the denominator and adds the numerator, keeping the denominator unchanged. 2
  • Carries out the return conversion and states that the two conversions reverse each other. 2

Part C 5

  • Identifies the first slip as adding where the conversion multiplies, and gives the correct improper fraction. 2
  • Identifies the second slip as writing the remainder over the numerator rather than the denominator, and says which way it moves the value. 2
  • States that the denominator fixes the size of a piece and that neither conversion re-cuts the pieces, so it cannot change. 1

General letters are one route to that; an argument in words that identifies the same exchange earns the same credit. 2
